interest: Shows 1941 FBI intelligence on the Yokohama Specie Bank's Hawaii branch moving assets to Japan ahead of freezing orders.
overview: January 1941 Hoover letter to Berle encloses an FBI memo: the Yokohama Specie Bank's Honolulu branch sought to shift notes, collateral, and deposits to Japan ahead of U.S. control, failed to liquidate $2.5 million in pledged bonds, and shared the strategy with mainland branches.

subfiles.about: Cover letter transmitting an FBI intelligence memorandum concerning the Honolulu branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends Berle a confidential January 1941 FBI memo on the Yokohama Specie Bank and its Honolulu branch.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr. transmitting FBI memorandum

subfiles.about: Confidential FBI memorandum detailing legal queries and asset transfer maneuvers by the Yokohama Specie Bank branch in Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: FBI memo: Honolulu's Yokohama Specie Bank branch sought to shift notes, collateral, and deposits to Japan, legal though inviting receivership; it failed to liquidate $2.5 million in pledged U.S. bonds, shared the strategy with mainland branches, and local Japanese residents bought certificates of deposit payable in Japan.
subfiles.title: FBI Memorandum on Yokohama Specie Bank Operations in Honolulu
